purpose: Historical regression replay proving the GC-010 T1J-R1-through-R3 chain under the SCEC standard, and why an unjustified narrow R4-style continuation is rejected once one reviewer scope expansion has already been recorded.
claimBoundary: Regression evidence only. Does not rewrite, reopen, or activate the historical T1J-R1/R2/R3 work orders or worker returns. Node hashes below are illustrative sha256-shaped placeholders for fixture testing, not the real committed file hashes.

chain.narrative: T1J-R1 identified that the approval-resume atomic-claim durable owner was undecided and left one bounded decision open for R2.

chain.nodeLabel: T1J-R2 worker: narrowed remainder to one connection-lifecycle gap
chain.narrative: T1J-R2 worker return selected terminal PARTIAL_READY_REQUIRES_FAILURE_RECOVERY_INTERFACE_DECISION, stating the CAS/crash-recovery design was sound and only SQLite connection-lifetime/storage-path ownership remained open (worker's stated single remaining gap). The durable-owner blocker is resolved and bound to the accepted R2 decision.

The reviewer's Independent Reviewer Correction rejected the worker's claim that connection lifetime was the only remaining gap: current /api/execute creates the NEEDS_APPROVAL response before the mandatory-gateway call, so the worker's assumed call order and payload provenance (originalGuardResult, environment, GuardPolicySnapshot) were not actually resolved. This is a reviewer scope expansion: reviewerScopeExpansions increments from 0 to 1, so under invariant 5 requiredDisposition escalates to ROOT_CONTRACT_REQUIRED and successorScope becomes INTEGRATED_ROOT_CONTRACT, not another INITIAL_BOUNDED single-gap decision.

chain.nodeLabel: T1J-R3 worker: narrow continuation despite standing escalation (the rejected pattern)

claims.evidenceRef: ApprovalStore.delete() single-winner pattern plus SQLite PRIMARY KEY constraint (worker's asserted two-mechanism proof)

chain.narrative: T1J-R3 worker return claimed route ordering and creation-identity uniqueness were now fully resolved with a two-mechanism exactly-once-creation proof, and selected terminal PARTIAL_READY_REQUIRES_ONE_NAMED_IMPLEMENTATION_PRECONDITION as if only SQLite lifecycle and recovery invocation authority remained. The route-order/payload blocker is moved to resolved WITHOUT any resolution-evidence binding, which invariant 13 now rejects as unsupported resolution laundering. This node's own requiredDisposition/successorScope (CONTINUE_BOUNDED / INITIAL_BOUNDED) is also INVALID under invariant 7: because reviewerScopeExpansions is already 1 from R2 and partialReadyClosures reaches 2 at this node, escalation was already required before this node was authored, so no successorScope may be INITIAL_BOUNDED here. This is the exact rejected pattern this fixture proves the checker catches.

chain.nodeLabel: T1J-R3 reviewer correction: same-claim correction plus continued escalation

claims.evidenceRef: reviewer rejects ApprovalStore.delete() as a single-winner barrier; only the SQLite PRIMARY KEY conflict path remains, and its conflict-before-provider-attempt ordering is undecided

chain.narrative: The reviewer's Independent Reviewer Correction rejected ApprovalStore.delete() as a valid single-winner barrier and named the consolidated owner-contract precondition. The reviewer also corrected the route-order/payload blocker back to retained: audit/consume ordering remains undecided and payload work remains blocking, so that blocker was never actually resolved. The accepted R2-to-R3 transition therefore grows the blocker set from three to four (three retained plus the rejected exactly-once barrier as new), and current contains four blockers. Because the accepted R1-to-R2 correction grew the blocker set from one to three and the accepted R2-to-R3 correction grew it from three to four, those are two consecutive non-decreasing transitions, so the stronger STOP_REASSESS_ARCHITECTURE / NO_SUCCESSOR terminal applies instead of another same-problem tranche.

chain.narrative: Even with executable proof declarations and a reduced blocker set, this same-problem successor is invalid because the accepted R3 predecessor already reached STOP_REASSESS_ARCHITECTURE / NO_SUCCESSOR after two consecutive non-decreasing transitions. Any architectural restart requires explicit operator authority and a new problem chain, not another T1J-R4 successor.

expectedCheckerOutcomes.r1_initial_node: PASS: valid INITIAL block, ordinal 0, no predecessor.
expectedCheckerOutcomes.r2_worker_node: PASS as a standalone block (ordinal 1, valid predecessor hash, valid set reconciliation, durable-owner resolution bound to accepted review evidence); demonstrates the worker's own narrow framing before reviewer correction.
expectedCheckerOutcomes.r2_reviewer_node: PASS: same ordinal 1 but corrected disposition; reviewerScopeExpansions=1 correctly triggers requiredDisposition=ROOT_CONTRACT_REQUIRED and successorScope=INTEGRATED_ROOT_CONTRACT per invariant 5.
expectedCheckerOutcomes.r3_worker_node: FAIL under invariant 7 (successorScope=INITIAL_BOUNDED is invalid once escalation stands from the predecessor chain state) and under invariant 13 (the route-order/payload blocker is resolved with no resolution-evidence binding).
expectedCheckerOutcomes.r3_reviewer_node: PASS: the corrected node retains all three R2 blockers (route-order/payload no longer resolved) and adds the rejected exactly-once barrier, giving current count 4; the second consecutive non-decreasing blocker transition requires STOP_REASSESS_ARCHITECTURE and NO_SUCCESSOR.
expectedCheckerOutcomes.r4_required_shape_node: FAIL: a STOP_REASSESS_ARCHITECTURE predecessor cannot have another successor in the same problem chain, even when the proposed successor declares executable proof with bound resolution evidence.
